newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, Raytheon sign $1.3 bln Sivam deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Raytheon sign $1.3 bln Sivam deal.

text.p: U.S. defence giant Raytheon Co and the Brazilian government have finally signed a contract for the controversial $1.285 billion Amazon Vigilance System (Sivam), Raytheon said.
Financing agreements for the deal, which had been held up for two years amid political wrangling and concerns over its cost, have also been finalized, Raytheon said in a statement.

As part of Brazil's plan to improve its surveillance of its vast and largely unchartered Amazon region, Raytheon will provide and install air traffic control radars, environmental monitors, meteorological radars and other equipment.
Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer will be responsible for air surveillance and remote sensing aircraft systems, the statement said.
The U.S. Eximbank provided loans worth $1.0 billion with the remainder being lent by Sweden's export bank, Raytheon and the Sivam Vendor Trust.
Sivam was due to fully operational within five years and will help Brazil protect the rain forest, improve air safety and border control and better plan land use, Raytheon said.
